workflowDefinitions.rationale: Start the EPIC clarification session; answer and completion applications resume its declared gates.
Start the FEAT clarification session; answer and completion applications resume its declared gates.
Collect readiness-approved context and generate the declared design artifacts.
Evaluate the structured worker outcome, route unresolved decisions to Deep-Dive, and promote only a completed result with valid artifacts.
Establish implementation prerequisites once and enter the shared phase executor.
Reconcile durable progress and re-enter the same shared phase executor.
Finalize evidence and lifecycle state only after all completion gates pass.

transitions.from: host verification execution or completion with declared non-applicable verification
transitions.trigger: phase evidence is written or consumed through the versioned JSON exchange
transitions.to: phase-specific gate projection or explicit protocol/evidence diagnostic
transitions.rationale: Use host-produced structured results and independent declared phase gates. Check configured identities, argv, working directory and required outcomes. Ordered task flags govern native applicability; the MCP Phase Quality Gate Contract governs compatibility applicability. Roles and file presence cannot add gates. Re-read applicability after developer revisions. Phase TwinTests do not replace EPIC workflow E2E obligations at their assigned checkpoints; mappings are many-to-many. Required failed checks and unresolved review findings remain blocked. Optional audit metadata does not gate decisions; migrated artifacts never fall back to prose success.

transitions.trigger: typed repair response requires schema and phase/task authority validation
transitions.to: independent host rerun, concrete blocker, or one bounded representation-only correction
transitions.rationale: Publish the same runtime schema to the worker, preserve execution facts through representation repair, forbid advisory acceptance for failed required checks, and report schema exhaustion as a protocol defect rather than a test failure. A worker repaired outcome is never evidence of passing tests.

transitions.trigger: before each provider request including continued tool turns
transitions.to: High-reasoning bounded request or terminal policy refusal without fallback
transitions.rationale: Apply locally tokenized context and independent token-spending admission to every Pi invocation. Bind the readiness output allowance only on supported transports; Codex subscription requests omit unsupported output fields and reserve catalogue maximum output consistently in planning and the wire guard. Resolve transport through the actual connection provider, never a feature/model name or display label. Use this reservation for 50/80 percent thresholds. Bytes are diagnostics, never tokens. Compact only losslessly at the provider boundary, never omit evidence or downgrade reasoning to fit. Resolve verified tokenizer capability before worker spawn; provider-qualified aliases select separately pinned tokenizer revisions. Readiness and request preparation share the resolver. Unknown selections report their identity before executing work; invalid assets never use estimated token counts.

transitions.from: current pack containing validated executable cases, possibly with incomplete overall coverage
transitions.trigger: Explicit human review of one case or all current validated manual cases, followed by observed pass/fail recording
transitions.to: Pack/review-bound case results; incomplete acceptance coverage still blocks feature completion
transitions.rationale: Manual case validity is independent of overall coverage. The user may review and record all validated cases in a current pack even while automated acceptance coverage is unresolved. Stale packs, invalid cases, partial reviews and failed findings remain guarded. Bulk recording persists individual case IDs and does not stamp completion or start finalization while overall readiness is incomplete. Top-of-dialog actions stay visible with reasons when disabled.

transitions.from: manual authoring interrupted after zero or more validated batches
transitions.trigger: human retries generation with unchanged sources, pack identity and guidance
transitions.to: remaining criterion batches assessed and saved before publishing a new pack
transitions.rationale: Persist validated batches independently of provider session timeout. Bind checkpoints to source/model and exact pack identity; stale inputs cannot reuse proposals. Drafts grant no acceptance authority. Invalid JSON or case-contract drafts are returned to the model with the exact diagnostic, rejected response and original source/guidance contract. Each correction rechecks source and operation ownership. Only validated replacements are checkpointed. Shared repeated-diagnostic detection stops repeated or cycling defects after three occurrences; provider/authority failures are not draft correction. Action prose is not restricted to a fixed opening-verb vocabulary; required fields, concrete context, placeholder rejection and human review remain authoritative.

transitions.from: current, stale or incomplete manual verification pack
transitions.trigger: human requests a new pack with optional scenario guidance
transitions.to: validated new version awaiting human review, or explicit unresolved coverage
transitions.rationale: Assess coverage and draft missing manual scenarios on every user-facing generation, even with blank guidance. Keep drafting separate from execution and acceptance; bind reviews/results to exact pack versions.

transitions.from: a still-owned phase recovery worker returns with a scoped verification diagnosis
transitions.trigger: validate the bounded handoff against exactly the selected criteria before automatic readiness refresh
transitions.to: source-bound diagnostic context for the next explicit repair, execution or investigation action; never passing proof
transitions.rationale: Preserve implementation/setup findings without treating missing execution as implementation authority. Actual executed failures may receive the explicitly scoped correction defined by the worker execution contract. Invalidate stale findings when cited sources or configuration change, preserve partial coverage, and prevent unchanged repair/investigation loops.

transitions.consoleCapturePolicy: Accept checksum-bound run-owned terminal stdout capture for test, static, preparation and discovery checks. Preserve equivalent literal invocation and exact cwd; a literal AND-list may be wrapped once in parentheses to capture the complete command. No added statements, changed selection, redirects or destinations. Native stdout log/text reports remain subject to native identity/count/outcome validation; health/discovery logs never prove test coverage. Importer verifies every supplied checksum and retains nonzero exits as failures.
transitions.executionProjectionPolicy: Allowlist executable check fields and source references for the execution prompt; omit planner reasons and phase prose. Receipt context separately allowlists id/kind/cwd/command so wider runtime objects cannot leak historical prerequisites into its identity envelope. Preserve original plan for audit/assessment. FV-21 proves both handoff boundaries and actual process execution using a controlled adapter; no guarantee of arbitrary live-model reasoning is claimed.
transitions.setupSourcePolicy: verification-setup/v2 requires inspection and execution to trace infrastructure and scenario state requirements to current runner/fixture code with exact references. Historical prose, cached reasons, previous receipts and sibling projects are not dependency authority. Use bounded runner-owned setup within existing permissions; report actual missing state controls separately. The inspection contract hash invalidates old baselines and triggers reinspection. This is a model instruction contract, not deterministic inference of arbitrary dependency graphs.
transitions.nativeReportCollectionPolicy: Inspect wrapper delegation before selecting commands: preserve scope/guards but use source-built native reporter checks instead of hidden no-build and summary-only output. Shared import accepts bounded reports path/sha256 collections or legacy report bindings, never both. Validate every native identity, count, outcome and checksum; console logs remain audit-only. Accept both hash-first and working-tree-first source qualifications, preserving the raw claim and rejecting multiple hashes. FV-19 and setup-contract scenarios exercise the corrections without weakening freshness or human acceptance.
transitions.commandResolutionPolicy: Before saving a baseline or dispatching execution, resolveVerificationCommands validates inspected and reused plans and binds the sole configured Cargo.toml when a built-in Cargo manifest-consuming command has no explicit manifest option and no discoverable manifest from cwd. Preserve flags, report destinations, cwd, test paths and phase mappings; reject ambiguous manifests. Record original plan and corrections; execution context, validation and future baselines use the corrected command. Never infer corrections from prior receipts or rewrite evidence. FV-18 and legacy-baseline HTTP coverage prove execution and reuse; optional receipt metadata remains optional.
transitions.commandPresentationPolicy: Shared binding compares literal POSIX/Bash arguments, assignment syntax and operators without executing shell text. Equivalent quotes, escaped spaces, continuation and separator whitespace are accepted directly, including with one literal cd to the configured cwd and separately bound console capture. Preserve raw receipt commands. Changed selection, argument boundaries, manifest options, report destinations, descriptors or control flow remain mismatches. Unsupported expansions/grammar retain exact-text matching and the existing diagnostic recovery path. No project or runner-specific rules.
transitions.receiptProductionPolicy: HEPHA normally includes runId in the current context/template and best-effort enriches missing receipt metadata after worker success, ownership and source checks, preserving receipt.worker.json. Missing/null/empty runId alone never blocks valid evidence, even when enrichment cannot persist. verifiedAt is optional audit metadata: absent, malformed, old or future values alone never block admission, and validation is independent of the current wall clock. Preserve raw timestamps; never invent replacements. Shared read-only import still validates current output directory, selected checks and native reports with source guards in the workflow. Explicit conflicting IDs remain errors. Adding metadata cannot certify execution. Current receipt contract is authoritative over historical examples. FV-10/FV-11/FV-12 cover normal production, conflicts and ID-less success; FV-13/FV-15/FV-16/FV-17 prove real execution reaches readiness despite timestamp errors and absent IDs through HTTP and browser Refresh. Legacy ordering of conflicting receipts remains unchanged. New workers receive the verification.execution.receipt common exchange schema and a host-owned receipt-template.json with fixed identities and null outcome placeholders. Runtime uses that same schema before independent native evidence checks; legacy receipt/v1 remains an explicit compatibility path. Resolve only HEPHA reserved output-directory placeholders to literal host-owned paths before execution and legacy receipt binding, preserving quoting semantics and unrelated expressions. No model correction or rerun is required for the expanded-path representation alone. Supporting artifacts (build provenance or diagnostic JSON) use checksum-bound artifacts entries and never supply test counts; native reports stay independently required.
transitions.planStabilityPolicy: FeatureDescription.md describes or links the current test inventory; test additions, renames and replacements update it together with configured selection. Persist a validated baseline, then revalidate identity, requirements, contract/project configuration, phase scope and content snapshots including dirty source and linked repositories. Unchanged plans retain selection with new run/report destinations; all tests execute again. Drift, corrupt data or unsupported snapshot context returns to inspection. Source drift during inspection stops before execution. No old report or acceptance is reused.
transitions.targetedCorrectionPolicy: Report original configuration errors with field/cwd/resolved path without cascading phase errors for existing references. Check ID order does not matter. Merge small checkUpdates/phaseUpdates for diagnosed entries, reject duplicate/unrelated/unknown fields, apply the full validator and persist. Complete plans remain compatible; runtime/cancellation bounds stay unchanged.
transitions.planOutputContractPolicy: Inspection and correction share one syntactically valid JSON template populated with required phase numbers. All example placeholders must be replaced by inspected configuration; the template itself grants no execution authority. The same parser and semantic validator admit both responses.
transitions.planFormatRecoveryPolicy: Presentation normalization distinguishes non-JSON inline code examples from competing JSON payloads. Malformed JSON gets a source-excerpt-free categorized diagnostic with line/column and recovery guidance, supplied with the saved response to bounded correction. Successful correction resumes actual test execution. Rejecting an unsafe candidate is not an immediate workflow stop.
transitions.evidencePipelinePolicy: Use readRecoveryExecutionEvidence for phase/repair and Refresh receipts. Refresh supplies current run/check bindings; no independent native-report validator or receipt schema is permitted. Current source snapshots remain mandatory. Successful non-test logs may be silent and never certify coverage. One parameterized execution prompt contract defines output for both callers.
transitions.planValidationPolicy: Locally decode one unambiguous JSON payload, allowing presentation wrappers but rejecting malformed/truncated/competing payloads. Apply the same semantic validator and persist the canonical selected plan; formatting wrappers alone never invoke correction. Classify test/static/preparation/discovery checks. Only actual tests claim automated gates and require test paths; non-test checks require successful bound logs and zero claimed tests. Reject identical canonical cwd/command executions. Shared files within a suiteKey are legal for distinct filters, assemblies, namespaces and configurations; the inspector compares actual selections before deduplicating equivalent or full/subset executions. Preserve every source reference. Typed unresolved plan and command-admission errors receive targeted corrections while validation progresses, each with a 180000ms worker runtime bound. The same diagnostic set recurring three times triggers escalation after root-cause diagnosis; distinct defects may continue. Cached plans pass the same admission before execution. Preserve raw output, canonical semantic candidates and aggregate diagnostics; instruct correction to preserve unaffected scope and avoid repeated inspection. Never retry runtime/budget/cancellation errors here. Targeted patches may correct either participant named by a duplicate or legacy overlap diagnostic; unrelated checks and phase obligations remain protected. Correction runtime failure retains the actual plan diagnostic plus runtime cause and points to Refresh Completion Readiness, without creating a phase finding or changing human results.
transitions.activityPolicy: Publish inspecting, correcting, preparing, testing, checking, waiting, validating and assessing from server-owned transitions. Track check identity through tool start/end including bounded newline/logging wrappers. Testing means active tests; supporting checks and waiting are separate, and completed attempts never imply passing evidence. Record correction category, attempt, reason and start time. Failed or interrupted runs clear active labels.
transitions.inspectionBudgetPolicy: Cumulative spending is operator-configured, never inferred from context capacity. Budget stops dispatch no tests/fallback. Preserve bounded partial inspection checkpoints for source-validated reinspection on a later explicit Refresh; never certify partial work or reuse it as execution authority.
transitions.scope: feature-wide fresh verification from user readiness refresh
transitions.from: idle implemented feature regardless of historical evidence or investigation gaps
transitions.trigger: user refresh explicitly carries reassess and verifyExisting authority
transitions.to: feature-wide inspection, fresh execution, source/report validation and assessment-only reconciliation
transitions.rationale: Every explicit Refresh verifies current source instead of trusting historical passes. Inspect all phase obligations, configuration and prerequisites; deduplicate shared checks and run all feature-related automation. Validate run-local native reports and unchanged repository snapshots. Failure, skip, missing report, interruption or source drift blocks readiness. Recover invalid evidence within the same run before assessment; no automatic production-code repair, approval or completion. Background assessment cannot dispatch workers. Explicit Refresh publishes schema-validated command-only inventory corrections and host-owned Phase references before capturing source baselines. Assessment-only calls do not write. Publication preserves criteria, flags, lifecycle and human results; cache reuse never replays old literal replacements.
transitions.linkedRepositoryPolicy: Command cwd and source ownership are independent. Existing relative configurationFiles bind their owning Git repositories, allowing matching testPaths across those repositories while preserving command, phase mappings and evidence obligations. Reject unbound source selections and symlink escapes. Enumerate configured directories through Git source inventory; validate containment and source existence without inferring runtime selection from shared files. Snapshot all bound source repositories during execution and baseline reuse. No new mandatory plan field or project-specific runner rewrite is introduced.
transitions.linkedRevisionPolicy: Fresh scoped imports may retain multiple explicit working-tree revision claims only when the leading full hash matches the command repository and every claimed full hash matches a configuration-bound source repository HEAD. Unbound, alternative, abbreviated multi-hash and legacy ambiguous prose remain rejected. Complete source-content freshness checks remain authoritative.
transitions.executionIdentityPolicy: Display names are labels, not globally unique keys. Retain every passing parameterized record with report-local references, preserve native TRX execution/assembly context and scope multi-report identities by checksum. Validate counts, all outcomes and native execution bindings; reject repeated report bytes and duplicate native execution IDs. Report-local references are not stable TestPlan IDs or proof of criterion coverage. Assessment matches the documented inventory, source assertions and configured scope; identical names cannot merge TwinTest and E2E evidence.
transitions.failedRefreshRepairPolicy: Project bound nonzero failed receipt checks through their inspected phase mappings, including when historical phase gates are satisfied. Revalidate commands and run-local report checksums server-side. User repair launches the generic historical-green discrepancy goal: trace task ownership, compare exact prior/current execution and dirty source/config history, repair correct production or incorrect test/scanner rules with regression evidence, and iterate until resolved or a concrete impasse/lack of progress. Successful fresh-failure repair return hands off to fresh verification; worker prose does not establish readiness. Other completed repairs reassess first and hand off to fresh verification when source changed; unrelated reassessment failures do not trigger execution. Preserve active-run/cancellation/successor guards and human acceptance.
transitions.nonTestConsoleCapturePolicy: Accept terminal checksum-bound log capture on the unchanged literal AND list for static/preparation/discovery commands. Preserve exit status and exact selection; earlier stdout is not claimed captured. Native stdout tests retain whole-list capture requirements.
transitions.evidenceRecoveryPolicy: Receipt/import validation diagnostics return to the verification agent with the exact rejection, selected plan and current native evidence. Correct recording defects without rerunning passing suites; rerun only unresolved selected checks and required dependencies when evidence cannot be recovered. Revalidate with the unchanged shared importer and source/ownership guards. Repeated or cycling diagnostic sets escalate on their third occurrence after a diagnosis attempt; changed audit metadata is not progress. Preserve rejected receipts and responses. No automatic production edits, plan weakening, human acceptance or lifecycle completion. Provider/budget failures remain distinct.
transitions.workerRecoveryPolicy: Recoverable inspection failures receive the original scope, saved inspection progress and exact failure before retry. Execution and evidence-repair worker errors return to receipt recovery with saved reports and the latest error. Reuse passing current-run evidence and resume only unresolved selected work. Shared progress policy detects recurring/cycling diagnostics. Explicit runtime-policy codes, exhausted provider routes, cancellation and spending/authority failures escape to their original owner.

transitions.explicitReassessmentPolicy: The single user Refresh first performs fresh feature-wide verification through WF-READINESS-EXECUTION-HANDOFF, then assesses all acceptance criteria using only current-run automated reports. Prior approvals remain historical and manual results remain saved. Background rechecks remain cached and never execute; confirmation and assignment cannot execute. Selected-model token and recovery policies still apply. Read-only coverage assessment is independent of manual-pack generation/review and unrelated phase/artifact blockers. A stale or absent pack excludes saved manual passes from current evidence but cannot suppress automated coverage assessment. Completion and coverage confirmation retain their separate freshness and authority guards.
transitions.modelCapacityPolicy: Resolve current local Pi SDK limits for every approved provider/model route once per refresh before planning; never use the display catalogue cache for compaction thresholds. Preserve 50/80 percent safeguards and fail closed on unknown live limits.
transitions.trigger: human selects Refresh Completion Readiness; pin exact provider-scoped SDK model limits and tokenizer; use a resettable 120-second idle watchdog without a five-minute absolute deadline; server-owned start, 50% light / 80% strong token occupancy compaction and settlement notify the board; spending limits remain independent; oversized fact arrays subdivide under a whole-refresh budget; importer-version changes invalidate former report exclusions
transitions.to: fresh assessment with criterion-group validation of mixed manual/automated evidence, retained partial proof and original diagnoses, grouped phase-owned gaps and optional unapproved coverage proposals
transitions.rationale: Opt-in recovery uses complete verified identities and authoritative human outcomes. Try lossless compression before retrieval. Inspect large source documents once in bounded pages, extracting exact additional operative clauses instead of whole related discussions. Validate page/criterion accounting, completeness, exact quotes and explicit duplicate occurrences. Preserve quote-local scope, offsets, source digest, negative qualifications and memberships; shared literal text cannot transfer authority. Bound page facts and per-criterion source context. Before buying identity retrieval, prove that source/manual/report context without identities can fit. Pack compatible criteria into bounded final groups while preserving the exact union of report-bound identity indexes. Share repeated diagnostic origins/reasons losslessly, retaining every occurrence and human result. Aggregate cross-page clauses and complementary evidence before a verdict. Plan below the runtime guard using local tokenizer counts, correction token headroom and an independent aggregate token-spending budget. Model context thresholds never use byte counts or the spending ceiling. Checkpoints bind full prompts and current algorithm/source/pack/report/result fingerprints and are revalidated on reuse. Incomplete or irreducible context remains an assessment error, never inferred test repair, permission to omit requirements or readiness. Completed assessment and explicit required coverage confirmation enable completion without rewriting manual package hashes or human results.
transitions.logicalCoveragePolicy: TestCoverage is logical alignment of current assertions, delegated fixtures and integration boundaries with accepted FEAT/EPIC criteria, independent of numeric telemetry. Reuse prior phase mappings with current source contents and fresh inspection findings. Passing execution and logical sufficiency remain separate; no line/branch/percentage report is required. Refresh inspects/runs/assesses without creating tests or fixing product code; an explicit phase fixer repairs confirmed in-scope findings and executes affected checks.

transitions.trigger: typed schema validation identifies an invalid field
transitions.to: same-evidence field corrections while validation progresses, then validated checkpoint or diagnosed impasse
transitions.rationale: Keep provider success distinct from valid assessment. Persist value-free field/type diagnostics and response hashes; never promote rejected output to evidence. Correction cannot drop evidence, relax coverage validation, execute tests or grant approval. A shared progress policy permits successive distinct field corrections; the same field and required shape recurring three times escalates after diagnosis. Response lengths, hashes and metadata do not reset progress. Each correction retains the full original evidence and prompt budget; transport failures do not trigger it. Validated checkpoints remain reusable across refresh and restart without repeating successful retrieval.

transitions.from: local or server-owned completion readiness refresh in progress
transitions.trigger: current card projection reports the recovery lock, including automatic refresh and browser remount
transitions.to: conflicting mutations disabled until both server and local activity settle
transitions.rationale: The authoritative recovery lock must drive the detail panel as well as the feature card. Disable refresh, coverage confirmation/assignment, phase repair/waiver, workflow and human-review mutations, manual results and generation, delivery preparation and EPIC relationship mutations. Preserve open drafts and read-only evidence/document/status navigation. Callback guards reject direct submission while busy; existing server guards remain authoritative for request races. Stale success notices and green completion styling cannot imply current readiness.

transitions.contextPolicy: Use the same pinned model token counter/capacity and shared spending budget as coverage assessment. Reserve output, framing, wrapper and correction room; apply 50% light lossless factoring and 80% strong criterion partitioning with a 75% target. Reuse bounded source-fact extraction only when needed; irreducible complete context remains blocked, never truncated. Group identical partial references while retaining distinct explanations and untouched approval bindings. Notify feature-card compaction activity. Compatibility-only injected runners without model metadata keep their conservative default bound.
transitions.from: new or cached unresolved coverage decisions
transitions.trigger: readiness refresh detects absent or changed configured action bindings
transitions.to: canonical existing execution targets or an explicit investigate-and-repair action
transitions.rationale: A separate bounded tool-free assessment selects only IDs from a statically discovered project catalog. Commands and paths cannot be invented by the response. Supply authoritative current pack/review-bound manual results, validated partial contributions and original diagnoses; historical phase prose cannot revoke these outcomes or reopen verified obligations. Preserve coverage proposals and all prerequisites, group shared runs, and invalidate saved bindings when configuration or normalized decisions change. Unsupported configuration is investigation work, not evidence of missing tests.

transitions.from: unresolved verification configuration or evidence mapping
transitions.trigger: human explicitly requests investigation and repair from the owning phase
transitions.to: scoped investigation, correction and affected verification, followed by automatic readiness reassessment
transitions.rationale: Unknown setup requires investigation first, not an inspection-only endpoint. The explicit repair includes all unresolved non-confirmation phase findings, prior diagnoses, configured targets and prerequisites. Correct verified in-scope gaps and execute affected checks while making progress. Historical generated inspection-only instructions cannot narrow this request. Preserve project setup authority, human acceptance, valid passing evidence, stale-document guards and cancellation. Assessment alone grants no repair authority.
transitions.repairSettlementPolicy: Explicit completed repairs reassess current evidence. If that reassessment reports the canonical changed-source condition, hand off to fresh verification automatically; unrelated failures and failed workers do not trigger execution. Cancellation and successor-run checks guard both handoff and result publication. Worker prose never grants acceptance.

transitions.from: identified existing tests without verified execution evidence
transitions.trigger: human makes listed prerequisites available and explicitly requests existing verification
transitions.to: execution-only preflight and report publication followed by automatic readiness reassessment
transitions.rationale: Typed execution requirements are untrusted preflight suggestions, not shell authority or proof. Surface prerequisites outside collapsed details; explicit phase execution requires acknowledgement, while the separate user Refresh handoff permits actual preflight without an availability claim. Worker checks real setup and stops if absent, without duplicate tests or production edits inferred from missing execution. An actual failing check may justify one in-scope correction and rerun with both reports preserved. Acknowledgement, discovery and worker prose cannot satisfy coverage. Verified imports and explicit confirmation still gate completion.

transitions.from: human-requested phase quality repair with a current terminal outcome
transitions.trigger: the repair worker settles without cancellation or superseding workflow
transitions.to: one server-owned readiness reassessment followed by a project-change notification
transitions.rationale: Repair completion must not leave readiness stale or depend on an open browser. Use fresh verification after a repair of bound failed Refresh executions; other repair kinds reuse assessment-only refresh. Neither path confirms proposals, alters results or finalizes. Independently check the selected gate after return: absent/failed execution or incomplete assessment records failed unresolved verification, not successful repair. Preserve repair failures and never overwrite successor runs.
transitions.failedRefreshRepairPolicy: Project bound nonzero failed receipt checks through their inspected phase mappings, including when historical phase gates are satisfied. Revalidate commands and run-local report checksums server-side. User repair launches the generic historical-green discrepancy goal: trace task ownership, compare exact prior/current execution and dirty source/config history, repair correct production or incorrect test/scanner rules with regression evidence, and iterate until resolved or a concrete impasse/lack of progress. Successful fresh-failure repair return hands off to fresh verification; worker prose does not establish readiness. Other completed repairs reassess first and hand off to fresh verification when source changed; unrelated reassessment failures do not trigger execution. Preserve active-run/cancellation/successor guards and human acceptance.

transitions.from: unresolved acceptance coverage or genuine task evidence after readiness refresh
transitions.trigger: explicit readiness refresh groups current evidence by verification responsibility
transitions.to: idempotent phase repair context and working phase controls; explicit repair dispatch receives the current server-owned gaps
transitions.rationale: Avoid per-criterion noise, navigation-only blockers and generic findings. Confirmation-only criteria are amber review controls, not repair instructions or red gaps, and cannot dispatch a repair worker. Reconcile exact terminal task evidence, assign generic verification ownership, exclude generated instructions from evidence and preserve human results. Only actual evidence or confirmed existing mappings can clear gaps.
transitions.presentationOwnership: Readiness summarizes phase gaps without duplicate phase action buttons. Artifact diagnostics use exact affected-document ownership and appear in that phase; unknown/feature ownership remains feature-level. Manual verification messages appear beside manual controls. No gate or authorization semantics change.

transitions.trigger: human explicitly confirms the displayed evidence links
transitions.to: audited coverage overlay and reassessed readiness; original pack and results unchanged
transitions.rationale: Validate known references and typed importer-verified provenance before explicit semantic confirmation. Isolate invalid proposed links by criterion while retaining unrelated valid proposals; malformed envelopes remain fail-closed. Exact source/evidence/outcome link bindings preserve unaffected confirmations after report changes, while changed links and source/package/algorithm changes require reassessment. Recheck during later scans and completion admission; no generated passing results, inferred code-review approval or implicit finalization.

transitions.from: in-progress feature with a resolved phase and an unresolved verification gate
transitions.trigger: explicit human repair request or confirmed, justified waiver for one selected gate
transitions.to: one bounded repair invocation with progressive scoped correction and verification, then independent reassessment; or an audited waiver without advancement
transitions.rationale: Instructions alone are not recovery controls. Preserve human authority with scoped worker dispatch, stale-document and active-run guards, and justified exceptions distinct from passing results. Reject known failed checks and rejected reviews on the waiver path. Cancellation remains authoritative. Other gates and human acceptance still block completion.
transitions.failedRefreshRepairPolicy: Project bound nonzero failed receipt checks through their inspected phase mappings, including when historical phase gates are satisfied. Revalidate commands and run-local report checksums server-side. User repair launches the generic historical-green discrepancy goal: trace task ownership, compare exact prior/current execution and dirty source/config history, repair correct production or incorrect test/scanner rules with regression evidence, and iterate until resolved or a concrete impasse/lack of progress. Successful fresh-failure repair return hands off to fresh verification; worker prose does not establish readiness. Other completed repairs reassess first and hand off to fresh verification when source changed; unrelated reassessment failures do not trigger execution. Preserve active-run/cancellation/successor guards and human acceptance.
transitions.repairSettlementPolicy: Explicit completed repairs reassess current evidence. If that reassessment reports the canonical changed-source condition, hand off to fresh verification automatically; unrelated failures and failed workers do not trigger execution. Cancellation and successor-run checks guard both handoff and result publication. Worker prose never grants acceptance.
transitions.logicalCoveragePolicy: TestCoverage is logical alignment of current assertions, delegated fixtures and integration boundaries with accepted FEAT/EPIC criteria, independent of numeric telemetry. Reuse prior phase mappings with current source contents and fresh inspection findings. Passing execution and logical sufficiency remain separate; no line/branch/percentage report is required. Refresh inspects/runs/assesses without creating tests or fixing product code; an explicit phase fixer repairs confirmed in-scope findings and executes affected checks.

transitions.from: a phase marked completed or skipped, before continuation or after worker return
transitions.trigger: persisted phase quality projection reports missing, unknown or unjustifiably waived evidence
transitions.to: same-phase evidence/code/test/review repair, followed by rescan and admission; escalate on repeated lack of meaningful progress
transitions.rationale: Every phase uses its declared independent review and meaningful-coverage flags plus configured checks. Canonical JSON overrides legacy result prose; native execution failures remain binding. Reconcile old evidence without inventing results, repair actual gaps, retain the original applicability baseline, prevent advancement outside the assigned phase and reassess repeated failures. Missing optional audit fields do not affect admission. Reject a disabled acceptance-coverage flag paired with an active assessment; reconcile scope without using numeric-threshold absence or reason-word matching as gate authority. Undeclared legacy gates require reconciliation independently of changed-file types. Coverage references may include passing supporting health checks when at least one behavioral test proves the criterion. Producers must not override declarations by project identity, phase position or work class.

transitions.from: admitted continuation or returned start worker with an isolated partial lifecycle transition
transitions.trigger: a closed read-only policy recognizes a stale Ready header or an unfinished authorized start move
transitions.to: same workflow resumes after verified repair, or blocks with a precise recovery rejection
transitions.rationale: One repair allowance per run: host repairs a known stale header; a missing start move gets one time-bounded agent attempt. Rescan must find one actual In Progress destination with valid artifacts and unchanged feature evidence. No repair may waive decisions, gates or phase authority. Read explicit status from header metadata or a relocated feature-identified metadata block, regardless of introductory headings. Reject competing declarations and do not borrow task, fenced example, quoted or commented statuses. Read-only validation never rewrites lifecycle metadata.

transitions.from: a bounded provider worker returns inside a durable user workflow
transitions.trigger: rescanned validated artifacts show progress and remaining work within recorded authority
transitions.to: a fresh phase session, finalization, supervised boundary, or an explicit blocked/failed outcome
transitions.rationale: HEPHA owns continuation across single-phase provider sessions. Explicit autonomy permits later phases and finalization; omitted or false autonomy stops at the selected phase boundary. Process exit zero is never workflow completion. Rescan and validate after each session, preserve cancellation and replacement, stop on real failure, block after two no-progress returns, and require completed artifacts before feature success.

transitions.from: validated compatibility documents at an admitted runtime boundary
transitions.trigger: a declared lifecycle folder alias is semantically equal to its canonical status
transitions.to: canonical feature-status projection with preserved phase evidence
transitions.rationale: Readiness accepts explicit known aliases without mutations. Execution writes canonical feature status only after validation and rejects contradictions with the actual folder. Phase headers and inventory rows must agree; unknown prefixes and nested status prose cannot satisfy the header contract. Dashboard recovery displays the actual implementation error rather than directing every readiness failure to Deep Dive.

transitions.trigger: validated recipe-source policy selects devcycle-mcp for the exact action identity
transitions.to: bounded plan-bound MCP compatibility sessions using mapped recipes under one durable workflow
transitions.rationale: Select the MCP recipe by action identity and preserve its exact server/tool/arguments across model routes. MCP responses are the sole procedural instruction authority: launch prompts carry transport, current validation diagnostics, session boundaries and host evidence/record locations, not duplicate verification, acceptance, test-plan, manual-test or gate-schema instructions. Provider-selected artifact validation, manual receipt persistence and deterministic gate admission remain host responsibilities; worker exit alone never proves acceptance. Native prompt policy and host-directed gate repair remain separate. The outer workflow preserves the authorized phase/feature boundary and resumes from rescanned evidence.

transitions.from: terminal MCP refinement worker with unresolved preparation lifecycle state
transitions.trigger: postcondition scan finds that the FEAT remains outside Ready To Develop after refinement
transitions.to: blocked result evaluation with interactive FEAT Deep-Dive recovery
transitions.rationale: A zero-exit model process is transport success, not refinement completion. When refinement cannot promote the FEAT into Ready To Develop because preparation decisions remain unresolved, preserve the worker summary and expose the standard interactive Deep-Dive recovery. A FEAT that is already Ready but has invalid provider artifacts follows WF-MCP-ARTIFACT-VALIDATION-FAIL instead so Refine remains available for deterministic repair.

transitions.from: terminal MCP refinement output or requested MCP Start/Continue action
transitions.trigger: the recipe-selected provider validator reports one or more refinement or implementation artifact contract violations
transitions.to: failed refinement result or refused implementation admission with exact deterministic diagnostics and no implementation side effects
transitions.rationale: Provider-specific format compatibility must not create split-brain readiness. The same selected validator decides whether Refine may complete, whether the dashboard may enable Start or Continue, and whether direct execution may proceed. Invalid Ready artifacts leave Refine available and inject the current diagnostics into the repair prompt. Start and Continue fail before recording a workflow run, creating a branch, dispatching a worker, or mutating manual-test state. Stable contract task markers provide identity; numbered headings and status prose are display content only.

transitions.trigger: deep-dive command accepted
transitions.to: question generation
transitions.rationale: Create one durable clarification session with one highest-priority opening question, then close every target decision through adaptive answer turns. Opening research uses progress-based inactivity liveness with no repository-default wall-clock maximum, so productive context inspection is not killed at the generic prompt timeout. Compatibility manifests are parsed without a hidden question-count ceiling, while the adaptive opening contract fails visibly unless exactly one question is returned.

transitions.trigger: questions persisted
transitions.to: waiting for human answers
transitions.rationale: Represent a human-input wait as durable workflow state rather than a failure.

transitions.trigger: one pending decision is saved
transitions.to: immediate dependent follow-up or the next pending decision
transitions.rationale: Evaluate each durable answer as part of the interview, insert an answer-dependent question immediately after its parent, and authorize document readiness only when the final answer closes the adaptive branch.

transitions.trigger: all answers are durable
transitions.to: updated source document
transitions.rationale: Rewrite the source only after the explicit Deep-Dive answer gate is satisfied, recording deterministic boundaries without future human-sign-off implementation tasks.

transitions.trigger: deep-dive worker or persistence fails
transitions.to: failed durable deep-dive session
transitions.rationale: Persist the failed clarification boundary so it can be diagnosed or resumed safely. Never replace a timed-out, failed, empty, or malformed model question manifest with generic Accept current questions that can falsely authorize an underspecified target.

transitions.trigger: backend authorizes a preparation action
transitions.to: visible preparation control and typed action dispatch
transitions.rationale: Render Design and Refine from authoritative action flags, independently of recovery diagnostics. Keep Refine disabled while required design is missing and retain voluntary Deep-Dive.

transitions.trigger: UI design is required
transitions.to: design artifacts ready
transitions.rationale: Produce design evidence only for features whose readiness policy requires it.

transitions.trigger: design agent or artifact persistence fails
transitions.to: failed design workflow with feature unchanged
transitions.rationale: Keep an unsuccessful design run auditable without falsely advancing readiness.

transitions.trigger: human requests additional exploration with optional focus
transitions.to: durable focused Deep-Dive interview
transitions.rationale: Clarification may be requested without validation markers. Persist focus separately from source, preserve existing interviews, reject conflicting active workflows, and enforce UI design prerequisites before provider-independent refinement.

transitions.trigger: one or more unresolved validation markers are present
transitions.to: Deep-Dive required until every marker is resolved
transitions.rationale: Require clarification only for explicit unresolved decisions; file hashes, lifecycle-link edits, metadata availability, and historical Deep-Dive receipts remain non-authoritative audit evidence.

transitions.trigger: refine command returns COMPLETED and durable artifacts satisfy the current V3 authoring contract; numeric coverage tooling is optional
transitions.to: ready-to-develop feature
transitions.rationale: Generate and validate the complete current implementation contract before promotion; historical contract readability cannot authorize obsolete new output. Carry the shared EPIC/FEAT/Phase/Task acceptance responsibility policy, many-to-many test/criterion/code traceability and assigned full-workflow E2E obligations through refinement. A final checkpoint role cannot introduce an LCOV profile or percentage requirement. Missing numeric instrumentation is not a Deep-Dive decision or a refinement blocker.

transitions.trigger: trusted Pi write/edit events or durable refinement artifact projection identify the current core artifact or contract-declared phase ordinal
transitions.to: active refinement with persisted user-visible artifact progress
transitions.rationale: Show deterministic core-artifact and phase progress from the selected FEAT folder and contract topology instead of opaque elapsed time or assistant prose.

transitions.trigger: configured no-progress stall, explicit operator maximum, process loss, or cancellation stops the worker before complete promotion
transitions.to: stopped refinement with source files preserved and resumable artifact position recorded
transitions.rationale: Preserve the primary stop cause and partial artifact checkpoint instead of hiding it behind route exhaustion or implementation-task recovery prose.

transitions.from: submitted feature with stopped refinement and partial artifacts
transitions.trigger: operator retries refine-feature with no active run or unresolved human/safety blocker
transitions.to: active refinement starting from the first missing or invalid artifact
transitions.rationale: Reuse valid core and phase artifacts, repair inconsistent output, and avoid replaying the complete handoff after a resumable interruption.

transitions.from: clarified or designed feature under refinement
transitions.trigger: refinement worker returns a valid NEEDS_DEEP_DIVE result with unresolved user-owned decisions
transitions.to: blocked refinement with an open interactive FEAT Deep-Dive question round
transitions.rationale: Preserve newly discovered planning questions as a durable human-input loop without misclassifying them as missing artifacts or failed refinement.

transitions.trigger: current Ready artifacts satisfy the refinement contract, architecture-debt readiness, source confirmation, and transition receipt even when worker transport or the Refine Feature Result V1 envelope failed
transitions.to: ready-to-develop feature
transitions.rationale: Recover from stale transport or result-envelope reporting failures without duplicating valid refinement work; readiness queries canonicalize independent selector order before the fail-closed store boundary.

transitions.trigger: worker result is malformed, Deep-Dive handoff persistence fails, or a COMPLETED claim does not satisfy the current V3 artifact and explicitly configured verification contract
transitions.to: failed refinement with source state preserved
transitions.rationale: Prevent incomplete planning artifacts from being promoted to implementation readiness.

transitions.trigger: start implementation accepted
transitions.to: branch verified and feature in progress
transitions.rationale: Establish the branch and lifecycle prerequisites before any phase work runs.

transitions.trigger: feature moved but implementation loop did not start
transitions.to: ready-to-develop feature
transitions.rationale: Undo a partial lifecycle move when no implementation work could have happened.

transitions.trigger: branch or lifecycle prerequisites cannot be established
transitions.to: failed start run without phase execution
transitions.rationale: Report prerequisite failure without pretending that the shared phase loop started.

transitions.from: idle, blocked, cancelled, or failed in-progress feature
transitions.trigger: the authoritative continuation contract is valid, unresolved work remains, and no workflow is running
transitions.to: continue implementation action available
transitions.rationale: Keep every stopped implementation resumable from the artifact contract owned by its selected recipe provider and project current-action readiness independently from Complete Feature obligations. Refinement-only satellites and diagnostics are not continuation authority; malformed native V3 or DevCycle lifecycle artifacts remain fail-closed.

transitions.trigger: continue implementation accepted
transitions.to: refreshed disk feature state
transitions.rationale: Resume from SQLite and MemoryBank evidence rather than stale in-memory state.

transitions.trigger: Continue Implementation reconciles phase documents, FeatureTasks projection, and SQLite task mirrors before task selection
transitions.to: reconciled durable feature state
transitions.rationale: Resolve and persist phase lifecycle state through one contract-aware projection before any implementation, review, or checkpoint worker is selected.

transitions.trigger: unresolved numbered phases exist
transitions.to: ordered phase queue
transitions.rationale: Select a generic phase path from durable contract state without feature-specific routing.

transitions.trigger: a completed legacy phase lacks required quality evidence
transitions.to: focused quality-gate recovery
transitions.rationale: Repair migrated durable evidence before ordinary phase selection.

transitions.trigger: declared human-review phase is pending
transitions.to: human review findings execution
transitions.rationale: Execute an explicitly declared human-review phase without confusing it with code review.

transitions.trigger: all declared phases are resolved
transitions.to: manual verification readiness
transitions.rationale: Stop dispatching workers when the phase contract has no unresolved work.

transitions.trigger: the authoritative phase-state reconciliation decision is all_terminal
transitions.to: completed implementation run awaiting Manual Code Review and Manual Tests
transitions.rationale: Finish a resumed run directly when reconciliation has already proved every declared task, required phase gate, and numbered phase terminal. A secondary scanner projection may present evidence but cannot reopen or veto this authoritative terminal decision.

transitions.trigger: autonomous mode has unresolved phase work and the run changed durable FEAT evidence
transitions.to: fresh Continue Implementation run
transitions.rationale: Create a successor only after a productive run crossed a durable boundary. Terminal reconciliation never reaches this scheduler.

transitions.trigger: autonomous mode still has unresolved phase work but the before-and-after durable FEAT fingerprints are identical
transitions.to: blocked implementation workflow awaiting an explicit user decision
transitions.rationale: Prevent equivalent fresh workflow runs from hiding an outer host loop. Persist the unchanged evidence fingerprints, preserve completed work, and let the user repair then Continue or Cancel without an arbitrary retry count.

transitions.trigger: durable phase evidence says resolved
transitions.to: next selected phase
transitions.rationale: Avoid repeating phase work already proven complete after a restart.

transitions.trigger: durable review state is the next declared task
transitions.to: review routing
transitions.rationale: Resume at review or fixer state without launching an implementation worker first.

transitions.trigger: next declared task requires worker execution and its zero-based non-negative phase identity satisfies the plan-bound runtime context
transitions.to: active phase worker
transitions.rationale: Dispatch exactly the first unresolved declared task and persist its active cursor; phase index zero is a valid contract identity rather than a missing positive identifier.

transitions.trigger: worker result is recoverably invalid
transitions.to: same task and same phase worker
transitions.rationale: Repair formatting, validation, build, or test failures without failing the whole phase.

transitions.trigger: task evidence settled and another task remains
transitions.to: next declared phase task
transitions.rationale: Advance only after the current task has durable evidence.

transitions.from: same-phase host transition requested after one recovery cycle
transitions.trigger: the before-and-after phase, route, decision, and durable FEAT evidence fingerprint are identical
transitions.to: blocked implementation workflow awaiting an explicit user decision
transitions.rationale: Attempt deterministic reconciliation once, then use unchanged before-and-after evidence rather than an arbitrary attempt count to prove no progress. Publish the exact route and fingerprint, preserve completed work, stop resource consumption, and let the user choose Continue Implementation after repair or Cancel.

transitions.trigger: Successfully measured FEAT changed-line coverage is below the advisory reference and the project coverage profile still allows another improvement attempt
transitions.to: same declared verification task after focused repair
transitions.rationale: Improve valuable FEAT-owned tests without expanding into unrelated project code. Percentage improvement attempts use the project-configured limit. Coverage execution or measurement errors record a non-blocking remark and do not enter this repair circuit.

transitions.trigger: coverage command, timeout, baseline, LCOV report, or instrumentation evidence is unavailable
transitions.to: completed verification task with a non-blocking coverage-unavailable remark
transitions.rationale: Coverage is developer decision-support telemetry. An inability to measure must remain visible without overriding independent green build, lint/typecheck, and test gates or failing the phase.

transitions.trigger: coverage commands and machine reports succeeded, FEAT and overall measurements were recorded, and either the FEAT reached its reference or the configured advisory improvement attempts ended
transitions.to: completed verification task and normal phase exit
transitions.rationale: Coverage percentages are quality telemetry, not lifecycle gates. The FEAT details retain the exact changed-line value and assessment while overall project coverage remains contextual.

transitions.trigger: review is required and no reusable approval exists
transitions.to: independent reviewer
transitions.rationale: Invoke one reviewer for the exact durable scope selected by the phase contract.

transitions.trigger: matching durable approval exists and rerun is not required
transitions.to: next declared task or phase exit
transitions.rationale: Treat an exact-scope approval as authoritative across process restarts.

transitions.trigger: draft review contract is repairable
transitions.to: validated review contract
transitions.rationale: Give the model one schema-grounded repair path before rejecting a useful review.

transitions.trigger: review contract remains V1 rejected after repair
transitions.to: blocked workflow
transitions.rationale: Prevent invalid review evidence from authorizing fixer work or phase exit.

transitions.trigger: review decision is NEEDS_CHANGES
transitions.to: fixer task
transitions.rationale: Route review findings to the fixer before any further reviewer invocation.

transitions.trigger: the existing NEEDS_CHANGES report has a complete Fixer Response and its canonical remediation response and bound verification receipt are durable
transitions.to: independent reviewer
transitions.rationale: Preserve the reviewer-owned NEEDS_CHANGES report, let the fixer update only its Fixer Response, and require a new independent reviewer report to decide whether remediation is sufficient.

transitions.trigger: review decision is APPROVED and its exact-scope authoritative gate is terminal APPROVED / approved_terminal_review
transitions.to: next declared task or phase exit
transitions.rationale: Advance sequentially only after authoritative terminal approval without inventing another review.

transitions.from: declared code-review task with nonterminal remediation authority
transitions.trigger: a remediation response lacks its bound verification receipt, or an APPROVED manifest is persisted with PENDING / terminal_remediation_required authority
transitions.to: fixer evidence recovery on the same declared review task
transitions.rationale: An unresolved declared task is a routing state, not a phase failure. Recover the incomplete response/receipt lifecycle before another reviewer or phase exit, preserving exact predecessor authority and task order.

transitions.trigger: recovered approval completes a declared review task and later tasks remain
transitions.to: next declared phase task
transitions.rationale: Preserve phase-file task order when approval is not the final declared task.

transitions.trigger: declared git checkpoint succeeds
transitions.to: completed phase
transitions.rationale: Record the immutable commit boundary requested by the phase contract; a retry publishes a previously sealed, reachable checkpoint without staging unrelated worktree changes.

transitions.trigger: declared git checkpoint fails
transitions.to: checkpoint pending
transitions.rationale: Keep implementation and gates complete while exposing a retryable git boundary; later unrelated work cannot invalidate a sealed checkpoint retry.

transitions.trigger: all declared tasks and required gates are satisfied
transitions.to: completed phase and next phase selection
transitions.rationale: Make phase completion the consequence of declared work and gates, not filenames, unrelated checklists, sign-off prose, or a continuation shortcut that bypasses phase exit.

transitions.trigger: observable current-worker stdout or stderr changes before the stall interval expires
transitions.to: active implementation Pi worker with a reset stall circuit
transitions.rationale: Keep productive multi-hour implementation alive without treating an estimated completion duration as a safety boundary; only observable current-worker activity resets liveness.

transitions.trigger: no observable current-worker stdout or stderr changes during the configured stall interval
transitions.to: terminated implementation attempt with the no-progress stall preserved
transitions.rationale: Detect a silent or hung worker promptly while refusing to confuse process liveness with progress.

transitions.trigger: an explicitly configured operator wall-clock maximum expires
transitions.to: terminated implementation attempt with the maximum-runtime cause preserved
transitions.rationale: Retain an optional absolute safety policy without imposing a repository-default deadline on productive implementation work.

transitions.trigger: failure is an incomplete fixer or code-review finding resolution
transitions.to: same fixer work retried
transitions.rationale: Retry remediation before review and preserve the required fixer-to-reviewer ordering.

transitions.trigger: the model provider rejects the accumulated worker prompt before the active task completes
transitions.to: same durable task through Continue Implementing in one fresh Pi session
transitions.rationale: Discard corrupted conversational state without discarding phase progress; one bounded Continue Implementing retry reconstructs the active task from durable evidence and a repeated refusal stops.

transitions.trigger: known deterministic host recovery can make the same task retryable
transitions.to: same phase retried with failure brief
transitions.rationale: Resolve known transport or durable-state issues without spending an agent turn.

transitions.trigger: recoverable failure needs bounded agent diagnosis
transitions.to: same phase retried or terminal failure
transitions.rationale: Use the model for diagnosis while keeping machine-owned state mutations guarded.

transitions.trigger: failure is fatal, explicitly blocked, non-recoverable, or retry is exhausted
transitions.to: blocked or failed workflow
transitions.rationale: Stop when another automatic attempt would be unsafe or unsupported and retain a durable brief. This ends the run, not the implementation: WF-CONTINUE-ELIGIBLE remains available when its durable continuation conditions hold.

transitions.trigger: user cancellation is allowed
transitions.to: cancelled workflow with settled phase metadata
transitions.rationale: Stop attached agents and settle durable workflow state so restart is safe.

transitions.trigger: user requests cancellation without an allowed active transition
transitions.to: unchanged durable workflow state
transitions.rationale: Reject cancellation when there is no active run or when its state cannot transition safely.

transitions.from: completed feature with resolved implementation phases
transitions.trigger: human generates a manual verification pack
transitions.to: SQLite-authoritative classified test delivery with executable manual cases or a Not Applicable informational artifact; feature remains completed
transitions.rationale: Treat completion as a lifecycle state rather than a filesystem freeze, so provider-completed and native-completed FEATs retain the same local verification workflow. Every criterion is classified Manual, Automated, Deferred, or Uncovered. Ready means at least one validated human-executable case exists; backend-only work instead receives a Not Applicable evidence artifact, and zero-discovery automated commands never count as passed coverage.

transitions.from: manual verification for an in-progress or completed feature
transitions.trigger: human records a failed manual test
transitions.to: finding recorded and feature lifecycle folder remains unchanged
transitions.rationale: Turn human-observed failure into durable remediation evidence without implicitly reopening a provider-completed FEAT.

transitions.trigger: all manual tests pass and completion gates are satisfied
transitions.to: complete-feature finalization
transitions.rationale: Start completion immediately after the last human gate becomes durable for a feature that is still in progress.

transitions.from: completed feature with a reviewed current manual-test pack
transitions.trigger: all manual tests pass
transitions.to: manual-tests green evidence recorded; feature remains completed
transitions.rationale: Persist post-completion green verification without launching Complete Feature for an already archived FEAT.

transitions.trigger: pack, review, test identity, or current-source binding is invalid
transitions.to: unchanged manual verification state with validation response
transitions.rationale: Keep stale or malformed manual evidence from authorizing remediation or completion.

transitions.trigger: complete-feature readiness accepts current evidence
transitions.to: detached completion finalizer
transitions.rationale: Create exactly one completion run only after code review and manual gates allow it.

transitions.trigger: complete-feature readiness rejects current evidence
transitions.to: unchanged in-progress feature
transitions.rationale: Refuse finalization until its declared completion gates are durable, while keeping those reasons isolated from current Continue Implementing readiness.

transitions.trigger: completion agent validates and moves the feature
transitions.to: completed feature
transitions.rationale: Finalize documentation, lessons, state, and folder movement through one auditable application.

transitions.trigger: completion agent or final state validation fails
transitions.to: failed completion run with feature not claimed complete
transitions.rationale: Expose finalization failure without falsely presenting a completed feature.

transitions.from: registered Web action with no persisted Global policy
transitions.trigger: the first policy resolution returns ROUTING_BOOTSTRAP_REQUIRED and Pi's explicit installation provider/model maps to one active cataloged connection
transitions.to: the same registered action resolved through one atomically persisted Global revision
transitions.rationale: Honor the zero-interruption bootstrap contract by supplying only Pi's explicit validated installation route after an unset-policy rejection. Never bootstrap display reads, replace invalid or unavailable persisted policy, infer from labels, or select an arbitrary fallback.

transitions.trigger: a future worker requires a route plan
transitions.to: typed accepted plan or deterministic rejection
transitions.rationale: Resolve only a registered action through persisted Action, Action Type, and Global policy before any execution boundary can consume a typed plan; a bootstrap conflict rereads the single persisted winner once and rejects absent, invalid, or registry-mismatched rereads without another mutation or execution.

transitions.from: accepted HandoffPlanV1 and guarded worker context
transitions.trigger: a worker-producing application invokes the required plan-bound runtime host
transitions.to: one pinned isolated primary Pi attempt with normalized lifecycle evidence
transitions.rationale: Consume the accepted route unchanged, pin connection and authentication versions before spawn, transport only the selected secret through the isolated child environment, and settle cleanup/receipt evidence without any model-key, default, policy, or substitute route lane.

transitions.from: malformed runtime input or an accepted plan with unavailable launch preparation
transitions.trigger: guard, connection, authentication, provider, vault, isolated-context, or process preparation rejects
transitions.to: sanitized no-spawn rejection or safe normalized preparation failure without an actual route
transitions.rationale: Fail closed before forbidden side effects for malformed input and never invent a route when valid-plan preparation cannot launch. Resolve ambiguous Pi-session endpoints only when exactly one authenticated provider identity matches, and preserve the failed route, durable cause, fallback availability, and routing recovery action in the surfaced error.

transitions.from: failed primary attempt with durable work state none and an approved second route
transitions.trigger: RuntimeExecutionCoordinator classifies the persisted primary state as none after failure, then invokes the approved second route with lifecycle hooks rebound to that fallback attempt
transitions.to: one fallback attempt on the unchanged approved second route; primary failure evidence remains durable and a successful fallback completes the invocation
transitions.rationale: Consume the plan-authorized second route once before substantive work without policy re-resolution, recursive routing, or a third attempt. Preserve the primary failure for explanation, but bind all fallback mutations and checkpoints to the fallback attempt so a successful fallback cannot be failed by stale primary state.

transitions.from: failed primary attempt with a durable checkpoint and unresolved task cursor
transitions.trigger: RuntimeExecutionCoordinator validates persisted checkpoint and no-replay facts
transitions.to: one recovery attempt carrying authorized checkpoint and completed-task identities
transitions.rationale: Resume from durable workflow evidence only; output text, elapsed time, task labels, and IN_PROGRESS alone never authorize recovery or fallback.

transitions.from: failed primary without a legal runtime hop or failed second attempt
transitions.trigger: the plan is exhausted, work started without a checkpoint, checkpoint evidence is malformed, or the second attempt fails
transitions.to: settled terminal invocation with no substitute or later workflow advance
transitions.rationale: Make no-step, Global, fail-immediately, unsafe recovery, and exhausted second-hop outcomes terminal instead of inventing a route or replaying work. Read already-persisted terminal attempts without settling them again; preserve policy-stop identity rather than creating a spurious persistence failure. Spending stops never buy a fallback.

transitions.from: portable skill invoked in an existing Pi, Codex, or Claude Code session
transitions.trigger: the user invokes the procedure directly without an explicit Hepha launcher or API dispatch
transitions.to: work remains in the current host with no routing-policy read, model switch, nested transfer, or orchestrated receipt
transitions.rationale: Portable procedure admission enforces model-neutral direct-host instructions, while production runtime composition exposes no direct-session route query, transfer adapter, or orchestrated receipt path.

transitions.from: direct-host procedure with an optional deterministic state-sync result
transitions.trigger: recordDirectHostRuntimeEvidence validates exact mode, project/card membership, registered descriptive action, and trusted model provenance before replay-safe persistence
transitions.to: one route-incapable direct-host evidence row and guarded mixed-mode FEAT Details projection, or deterministic rejection with no orchestrated receipt
transitions.rationale: Direct evidence records host work honestly without granting routing authority: exact replay is a no-op, collisions reject, untrusted model claims reject, and policy, route, authentication, credential, launch, attempt, and fallback facts are structurally unavailable.

transitions.from: dashboard or specialist launch request carrying one explicit agent_action
transitions.trigger: AgentTaskRuntime.create or SpecialistRuntimeDispatchApplication.execute validates action syntax, registry membership, launch-node equality, and complete registry-plan metadata
transitions.to: one registry-bound immutable plan, or deterministic rejection before task numbering, persistence, coordinator execution, or spawn
transitions.rationale: Action identity is serialized authority; command names, filenames, roles, skills, models, and route fields cannot infer or override it.

transitions.from: parent invocation and scoped nested action request
transitions.trigger: the production review, phase-exit, feature-lessons, or successful post-complete lifecycle entry admits its exact action and a real current-run parent invocation exists
transitions.to: separate nested chain with primary first attempt and durable parent/root/correlation/input lineage; failed completion starts no curator
transitions.rationale: With a real current-run parent, Code Review and all three knowledge workers inherit correlation and scoped artifact references only, never the parent route, retain sorted selected lesson identities, and keep curator effects project-only. The nested adapter requires complete action/type/role/prompt/capability equality with the registry before invocation identity or coordinator work. A resumed specialist with no parent uses WF-RUNTIME-RESUMED-SPECIALIST instead.

transitions.from: resumed workflow whose first model invocation is a declared specialist action
transitions.trigger: the production specialist boundary has an independently accepted plan but no real root invocation exists for the current workflow run and card
transitions.to: one fully scoped root specialist chain carrying the current workflow, card, phase contract, phase, and task identity
transitions.rationale: Represent the actual resumed topology honestly: use nested dispatch only with a real current-run parent, and never invent a context-free parent receipt merely to satisfy nested lineage.

transitions.from: terminal primary or plan-authorized second attempt
transitions.trigger: the executor or coordinator commits terminal attempt and route-change evidence
transitions.to: immutable canonical invocation settlement available after restart
transitions.rationale: Keep the final attempt and event result authoritative, monotonic, conflict-safe, and readable as normalized evidence without legacy telemetry inference.

transitions.from: completed fixer output after one ## Fixer Response was appended or updated in the existing NEEDS_CHANGES report
transitions.trigger: the output contains one exact remediation-response block and one verification-receipt block bound to the immutable NEEDS_CHANGES predecessor
transitions.to: durable remediation response and bound verification receipt, or same-fixer repair with a sanitized validation diagnostic
transitions.rationale: The reviewer-owned report and NEEDS_CHANGES decision remain immutable; the fixer updates only the report's single Fixer Response section. A fixer proposal is not review authority. The independent reviewer may run only after the canonical nested response schema and complete receipt are persisted. Invalid model output must return the contract rejection code/message so a retry can change the malformed field instead of repeating an opaque failure.

transitions.from: phase evidence scan or declared verification task return
transitions.trigger: explicit applicability flags and observed command outcomes are evaluated
transitions.to: phase acceptance governed by required tests and code review, with optional health-warning repair
transitions.rationale: Read portable boolean Phase Gate Declarations when no canonical gate record owns applicability. Never infer from identity or changed files. Preserve independently configured test failures. Build/lint outcomes remain truthful advisory warnings and cannot manufacture missing coverage, block phase advancement or launch unsolicited repair. Canonical gate records retain revision validation. Human-requested health repair remains available on the phase. A required-review declaration defers to indexed report verdicts rather than replacing approval with a missing placeholder.

transitions.from: current feature planning baseline and applicable verification evidence
transitions.trigger: authorized completion readiness assessment or post-repair reassessment
transitions.to: validated criterion decisions, scoped repair or verification retry, and non-blocking future proposals
transitions.rationale: Assess only accepted feature obligations and assigned parent criteria. Validate one versioned JSON exchange against the host baseline; complementary proof is valid without coverage-link confirmation. Read missing references within admitted roots, preserve manual outcomes and native report binding, and keep extra improvements outside current gates. A validated unmet obligation cannot be overwritten by legacy worker diagnosis routing.

transitions.trigger: explicit user Refresh with unchanged source and independently valid selected reports
transitions.to: resume the same execution run and assess accepted feature criteria without test redispatch
transitions.rationale: Revalidate every selected receipt, source owner and snapshot before resuming interrupted validation. Audit-only duplicate bindings count no tests. Qualified multi-repository revisions bind to configured owners. Failed or stale evidence does not resume; human acceptance remains independent.

transitions.from: accepted feature criteria, automated evidence and independent human acknowledgements
transitions.trigger: completion readiness assessment or projection
transitions.to: automated criterion decisions plus separate human acknowledgement blockers
transitions.rationale: Manual cases and results never supply automated coverage or invalidate its cache. Manual acknowledgement remains a required independent completion step. Explicit manual-only obligations do not manufacture automated requirements. Preserve existing human records and reject manual contributions in the v2 exchange.

transitions.from: validated accepted criteria with pending assertion references
transitions.trigger: read-only evidence retrieval during readiness assessment
transitions.to: retained decisions and accumulated source context for unresolved criteria
transitions.rationale: Retain all retrieved source bodies and validated decisions on an unchanged snapshot. Follow new references while context and operator spending limits permit progress, rather than stopping after two hops. Resolve document anchors within the admitted feature folder and source roots. Assess the accepted collective verification approach without adding test layers or replacing manual-only qualifications. Repeated or unavailable references remain verification issues, not passes or missing implementation findings.

transitions.from: fresh verification source snapshot changed after execution
transitions.trigger: same explicit Refresh retains ownership and accepted feature requirements are unchanged
transitions.to: diagnose changed files, re-inspect setup and rerun all checks in a new attempt; assess only after stable snapshots and valid reports
transitions.rationale: A configured runner can regenerate tracked inputs. Never waive fingerprint checks or promote old reports. Persist filename/hash diagnostics, preserve each attempt, prohibit dropped checks/gates/phase assignments, and allow two automatic reinspections and executions. After three drifting executions stop with a browser Retry verification action. Requirements changes and cancellation remain boundaries. No generated filename or project type is special-cased.

transitions.trigger: host reassessment finds the selected gate, health warning or phase completion gap still unresolved
transitions.to: feed current evidence and prior worker report into the next scoped repair; verify again; escalate after three unsuccessful rounds
transitions.rationale: Worker return is not repair success. The same selected scope and user guidance own up to three repair-and-verification rounds. Keep health warnings non-blocking for overall completion but require their resolution when explicitly selected for repair. An unavailable assessment cannot establish a repair postcondition. Source-invalidated repairs hand off to owned fresh verification. Preserve cancellation, human decisions, independent approval and existing fresh-verification ownership. Escalation reports each round, unresolved evidence and how the phase textbox can steer another loop.
